subproblem.title: Boundary commutes with smooth push-forward (Simon 2.24(1))
subproblem.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^Q, X ∈ D_{k+1}(U), S ∈ D_{k+1}(V), and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be of class C^∞. Suppose S(ω′) = X(η′) whenever ω′ ∈ D^{k+1}(V), η′ ∈ D^{k+1}(U) and η′ = f^#ω′ on some open set containing spt X. Then ∂S(ω) = ∂X(η) whenever ω ∈ D^k(V), η ∈ D^k(U) and η = f^#ω on some open set containing spt X. Here (f^#ω)(x) := ω(f(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (Df(x)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V (k + 1)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ (ω : TestFormOn V (k + 1)) (η : TestFormOn U (k + 1)), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (k + 1)) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) (k + 1)) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S ω = X η) → ∀ (ω : TestFormOn V k) (η : TestFormOn U k), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) k) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S.boundary ω = X.boundary η
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (Simon 2.24(1): ∂f_#T = f_#∂T), with the degree-(k+1) formula as hypothesis. The formula is applied directly to dω and dη on the same open set. This shortens the parent's step 5, which goes through an auxiliary η′ from (F5) and the support fact (F2); neither is needed.

Notation:
- p_ω(x) := Df(x)^#(ω(f(x))) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x);
- for ψ ∈ D^k(U) (resp. D^k(V)), dψ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k ψ ∈ D^{k+1}(U) (resp. with V); its underlying form is extDeriv ψ;
- by definition ∂S(ω) = S(dω) and ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply).

1. Fix ω ∈ D^k(V), η ∈ D^k(U) and an open N ⊇ spt X with η(x) = p_ω(x) for every x ∈ N. Then dω ∈ D^{k+1}(V) and dη ∈ D^{k+1}(U).
2. (Locality.) Let x ∈ N. Since N is open, η = p_ω on a neighbourhood of x, i.e. η =ᶠ[𝓝 x] p_ω (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Hence extDeriv η x = extDeriv p_ω x (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq): extDeriv ψ x is the alternatization of fderiv ℝ ψ x, which depends only on the germ of ψ at x.
3. (Naturality.) ω is C^∞, being a test form, so it is differentiable at f(x). f is C^∞, so ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ f x, and minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2 ≤ ∞. Mathlib's extDeriv_pullback therefore gives
   extDeriv p_ω x = (extDeriv ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) = Df(x)^#((dω)(f(x))).
4. By steps 2–3, (dη)(x) = Df(x)^#((dω)(f(x))) for every x ∈ N. So dη agrees with the pull-back of dω on the open set N ⊇ spt X. The hypothesis, applied with ω′ := dω, η′ := dη and the same N, gives S(dω) = X(dη).
5. Hence ∂S(ω) = S(dω) = X(dη) = ∂X(η). ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂S(ω) = S(dω) and ∂X(η) = X(dη) by the definition of the boundary.
Locality of extDeriv on the open set N where η = f^#ω, together with Mathlib's extDeriv_pullback (naturality of d), gives dη = f^#(dω) on N.
Applying the degree-(k+1) formula to (dω, dη, N) gives ∂S(ω) = X(dη) = ∂X(η).

audit.reason: The higher-degree formula is an explicit hypothesis, so no child dependency is missing. Locality and extDeriv_pullback establish compatibility of dη and dω on the same neighbourhood. Applying that hypothesis and boundary_apply proves the exact conclusion without circularity or additional properness assumptions.

subproblem.title: Compatible compactly supported pull-backs exist (cut-off of Simon 2.23)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), IsOpen U → A ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ A)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn V j, ∃ (η : TestFormOn U j) (ζ : Eucl P → ℝ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen N ∧ A ⊆ N ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ζ x ∧ ζ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ζ x • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) ⊆ f ⁻¹' tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F5) of the parent proof (the cut-off function ζ of Simon 2.23, p. 139), filled in. It is stated for an arbitrary set A ⊆ U on which f is proper; the parent uses A = spt X. Neither MapsTo nor openness of V is needed.

Notation: p(x) := Df(x)^#(ω(f(x))) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) is the pull-back form f^#ω. C^∞ means smoothness of order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. of every finite order.

1. (The compact set.) ω ∈ D^j(V) has compact support, so tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport.isCompact), and tsupport ω ⊆ V. By the properness hypothesis, K := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A is compact, and K ⊆ A ⊆ U.
2. (Thickenings.) K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is δ₀ > 0 with cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Define:
   - O := thickening (δ₀/2) K, open, with K ⊆ O (self_subset_thickening, as δ₀/2 > 0);
   - C := cthickening (δ₀/2) K, closed, with O ⊆ C (thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - s := thickening δ₀ K, open, with C ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ₀ and δ₀/2 < δ₀).
   If K = ∅, all these sets are empty and the argument below still applies.
3. (The cut-off.) Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with n = ⊤, applied to the open set s and the closed set C ⊆ s) gives a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], support ζ = s, and ζ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ C. Consequently:
   - 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 everywhere, and ζ = 1 on O;
   - tsupport ζ = closure s ⊆ cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - cthickening δ₀ K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so its closed subset tsupport ζ is compact, i.e. ζ has compact support.
4. (p is C^∞.)
   - x ↦ Df(x) is C^∞ because f is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right, using ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞).
   - x ↦ ω(f(x)) is C^∞ as the composition of the C^∞ maps ω (a test form) and f.
   - B ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM B is C^∞. It sends a continuous linear map B : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap B on j-covectors, and it is analytic on the whole space (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiff).
   - Since p(x) = (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Df(x)))(ω(f(x))), p is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.clm_apply).
5. (The test form.) Define η(x) := ζ(x)·p(x). η is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul). Also tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ (tsupport_smul_subset_left), so η has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right) and tsupport η ⊆ U by step 3. Hence η ∈ D^j(U) = TestFormOn U j, and η(x) = ζ(x)·p(x) for all x by definition.
6. (Support.) If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(f(x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence p(x) = 0, the pull-back of the zero covector being zero, and η(x) = 0. So support η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω). This set is closed, since f is continuous and tsupport ω is closed, so tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) (closure_minimal).
7. (The open set.) Put N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), an open set. A ⊆ N: for x ∈ A, if f(x) ∈ tsupport ω then x ∈ K ⊆ O; otherwise x ∈ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω).
8. (η = p on N.) If x ∈ O ⊆ C, then ζ(x) = 1 and η(x) = p(x). If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then p(x) = 0 = η(x) by step 6.
9. Steps 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 show that η, ζ and N have all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Properness makes K := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A a compact subset of the open set U.
Smooth Urysohn on thickenings of K gives a C^∞ cut-off ζ with values in [0, 1], compact support in U and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood O of K.
The pull-back p = f^#ω is C^∞ (B ↦ B^# is analytic), so η := ζ·p ∈ D^j(U) with tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω).
η = p on the open set N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), which contains A.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and requested properties match. Properness produces the compact set; thickenings and smooth Urysohn provide the cutoff. Analyticity of linear pullback establishes smoothness, and the closed preimage argument establishes topological support containment. The neighbourhood covers A, including the empty-compact-set case.

subproblem.title: Pull-back of covectors: |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j |α| for the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (L : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q) (α : Covector (Eucl Q) j), covectorEuclideanNorm (α.compContinuousLinearMap L) ≤ ‖L‖ ^ j * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F3) of the parent proof. The parent justifies (F3) by the singular value decomposition. Transferring that argument to covectorEuclideanNorm, which is defined on continuous alternating maps through the standard basis, would need an SVD factorization L = Σ_i σ_i u_i ⊗ v_i and the orthonormality, for this norm, of the wedges of an arbitrary orthonormal basis. The pinned Mathlib has singular values (LinearMap.singularValues) and an inner product on the abstract exterior power ⋀[ℝ]^n E, but neither the factorization nor any link to covectorEuclideanNorm. The same inequality is therefore proved by the elementary tensor (Hilbert–Schmidt) argument below, which uses only the standard bases.

Notation:
- e_1, …, e_P and e′_1, …, e′_Q are the standard orthonormal bases of ℝ^P and ℝ^Q (EuclideanSpace.basisFun);
- for i : Fin j → Fin P, e∘i := (e_{i(1)}, …, e_{i(j)}), and similarly e′∘i for i : Fin j → Fin Q;
- |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ, so for a j-covector γ on ℝ^m (m ∈ {P, Q}, with the corresponding standard basis), |γ|² = Σ_{I : Fin j → Fin m strictly increasing} γ(e∘I)²;
- L^#α := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (L^#α)(v₁, …, v_j) = α(Lv₁, …, Lv_j);
- |·| on vectors is the Euclidean norm, ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product, and ‖L‖ the operator norm.

1. (Sum over all index tuples.) For every j-covector γ on ℝ^m: Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} γ(e∘i)² = j!·|γ|².
   (a) If i is not injective, e∘i has two equal entries, so γ(e∘i) = 0 because γ is alternating.
   (b) The map (I, σ) ↦ I ∘ σ is a bijection from pairs (I strictly increasing Fin j → Fin m, σ a permutation of Fin j) onto the injective maps Fin j → Fin m.
      - Surjectivity: for injective i, the tuple i ∘ (sort i) is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing. With I := i ∘ sort i and σ := (sort i)⁻¹, I ∘ σ = i.

subproblem.title: The Lipschitz push-forward of 3.6 is the classical push-forward for differentiable maps
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), Differentiable ℝ f → IsLipschitzPushforward X f S → ∀ (ω : TestFormOn V n) (η : TestFormOn U n), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) n) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S ω = X η
proof_key_steps: Unfold IsLipschitzPushforward: X = τ(M, θ, ξ), f has tangential directional derivatives L(x)v a.e., and S(ω) = ∫_M θ (L_#ξ)(ω∘f) dHⁿ.
By the sibling support-null lemma, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. point of M lies in spt X ⊆ N.
At such points, uniqueness of the derivative of t ↦ f(x + tτ_i) gives L(x) ∘ τ = Df(x) ∘ τ on the orienting frame. Hence (L(x)_#ξ(x))(ω(f x)) = ξ(x)(Df(x)^#ω(f x)) = ξ(x)(η(x)).
The integrands of S(ω) and X(η) agree a.e. on M, so S(ω) = X(η) by integral_congr_ae.
